label: unrelated
point: The Court held Texas Districts 18, 29 and 30 were racial gerrymanders failing strict scrutiny; the VRA (including § 1973a) is cited only as background.
why: The terminology change about federal observers has nothing to do with the decision's equal-protection holding; the report names Bush v. Vera only in passing about DOJ max-black-district objections.

label: unrelated
point: The dissent from denial of rehearing en banc cited § 2251(a) in passing as a statute a court read a scienter/reasonable-mistake requirement into, while criticizing § 2257 record-keeping rules.
change: The law changed the penalty cross-reference in § 2251(a) from subsection (d) to subsection (e) after redesignation.
why: A cross-reference renumbering does not touch anything the decision did with § 2251(a); the report names the panel decision (33 F.3d 78) in the same case, only to describe § 2257 as upheld.

label: related
point: The Court held that under FAA § 2 a challenge to the validity of the whole contract (under California's Talent Agencies Act) goes to the arbitrator, and the FAA overrides state rules giving an administrative agency primary jurisdiction.
change: The EFAA added 'or as otherwise provided in chapter 4' to § 2, making predispute arbitration agreements unenforceable at the claimant's election for sexual assault and sexual harassment disputes.
why: The change limits § 2 for a different class of disputes and would not alter the result on who decides a talent-agency validity challenge; the report cites Preston only as an example of FAA preemption.

label: codifies
point: The court held that § 1001 reaches false statements and omissions in Ethics in Government Act financial disclosure forms filed with the House, because 'department' includes the legislative branch.
change: The False Statements Accountability Act rewrote § 1001 to cover matters within the jurisdiction of the executive, legislative, or judicial branch, with legislative-branch coverage limited to administrative matters including documents required by law to be submitted to Congress, and added materiality to each clause.
why: After Hubbard rejected the Bramblett reading Hansen relied on, Congress restored legislative-branch coverage expressly including documents required by law to be filed with Congress, so Hansen's result on EIGA filings is written into the statute; the report cites Hansen approvingly.

label: codifies
point: The court held that Coltec's capital loss, though within the literal terms of the Code, arose from a transaction lacking economic substance and must be disregarded.
change: In § 105 the law extended employer health reimbursement exclusion to children under 27; elsewhere the same law (new § 7701(o)) codified the economic substance doctrine.
why: The § 105 change is unrelated, but the law codifies the economic substance doctrine Coltec applied and the report cites Coltec as an example of the doctrine as courts apply it.

label: unrelated
point: The court reversed a § 924(c) conviction because the jury was not instructed that the firearm must be related to the underlying felony (and vacated a CCE life sentence).
change: The law added 'firearms possession (as described in section 924(c))' to the § 3559(c) list of serious violent felonies, as a conforming change to the new possession-in-furtherance offense.
why: The three-strikes list change has no bearing on the decision's 'in relation to' point, which Congress left intact for use/carry; the report cites Stewart (via Smith) only for the meaning of 'during and in relation to'.

label: related
point: The court denied summary judgment, holding that ringless voicemails delivered to a cell phone are 'calls' using an automatic dialing system or prerecorded voice subject to TCPA § 227(b)(1)(A)(iii).
change: The TRACED Act added FCC civil forfeiture authority to § 227(b) and required FCC exemptions under (b)(2)(B)/(C) to limit callers, called parties and call numbers.
why: The amendments strengthen robocall enforcement on the same subject but do not change whether ringless voicemails are covered calls; the report cites Saunders only as an example of courts so holding.

label: related
point: The panel held the government stated a reverse false claim under § 3729(a)(7) by alleging Pemco's false inventory record concealed or decreased an obligation to pay or transmit property to the government.
change: FERA restructured § 3729(a), moving the reverse false claim to (a)(1)(G), adding liability for knowingly concealing or improperly avoiding an obligation, requiring materiality, and defining 'obligation'.
why: The amendments broaden the reverse false claims provision and would not lead to a different result on Pemco's point; the report cites the en banc decision in the same case only among circuit cases on the provision.

label: related
point: The court held that a district-court-appointed interim United States Attorney under § 546(d) lawfully holds office until the vacancy is filled, even after six years, and the statute is constitutional.
change: The 2007 Act restored § 546(c)(2) and (d), reinstating the 120-day limit on Attorney General interim appointees and district court appointment thereafter, which the 2006 law had removed.
why: The law restores the court-appointment scheme Hilario upheld rather than changing its rule; Hilario is cited only in minority views to argue the executive holds the trump cards.

label: codifies
point: The Court held that the OWCP Director is not a 'person adversely affected or aggrieved' under LHWCA § 21(c) and so lacks standing to seek review of Benefits Review Board decisions.
change: No words of the linked § 1011 changed; the appropriations law bars the Solicitor of Labor from using funds to participate in court of appeals review of Board decisions where the Supreme Court's decision precludes such participation.
why: The rider names the decision and builds on its limit rather than reversing it, so Congress accepts the holding; the linked Title 16 section is unrelated.
